HomeSteadyLink — full product details
=====================================

What it is
----------
HomeSteadyLink is a BLE-provisioned travel router built on the Orange Pi
Zero 2W. At first boot a phone app pushes Wi-Fi credentials to the device
over Bluetooth Low Energy; the device joins the Wi-Fi network and brings
up a VPN behind a kill switch. It is a travel router: one device that
connects to hotel, cafe, or home Wi-Fi and puts everything behind it on
a VPN.

The downloadable product is the Android app (Google Play, Android only).
The app configures the device. iOS source exists; App Store publish is
out of scope. The product is in alpha with a bunch of alpha testers right
now and expanding soon. The website's primary action is joining the
waitlist; the Play app installs and configures the device. Pre-orders
open when the firmware is delivered and the app is verified on real
hardware — nobody pays yet.

Two control paths, one product
------------------------------
1. Android app over BLE (the main path): scan, pair, Wi-Fi, VPN,
   progress, device dashboard. The phone app pushes Wi-Fi credentials
   over BLE at first boot. Source: https://github.com/HomesteadLink/mobile-app
2. Web app over USB (WebUSB, the second path): connect over a USB cable,
   list Wi-Fi networks and connect, set up the VPN (WireGuard or
   Tailscale with an exit node), progress, device. Live at
   https://homesteadlink.github.io/web-app/ — a single-file static app
   (index.html, plain JavaScript + WebUSB, no build step).
   Source: https://github.com/HomesteadLink/web-app

There is no setup code anywhere in the web-app flow: physical USB
presence is the trust root. The setup code stays for BLE only.

Requirements
------------
Web app browsers: Chrome and Edge on macOS, Windows, and Linux; Android
Chrome with a USB cable. Safari and Firefox have no WebUSB — the fallback
is the router's Wi-Fi setup page at http://192.168.65.1:8080.

The Android app needs a real board and a real phone for its physical
test session (checklist P1–P16). Screenshots for the Play listing come
from real tested flows, never mockups.

Firmware and hardware
---------------------
Firmware runs on the Orange Pi Zero 2W and is built from the committed
tree; the delivered image is a provenance-stamped artifact with size and
SHA-256 recorded. Source: https://github.com/HomesteadLink/firmware

- v1.3 delivered publicly 2026-11-16 as a GitHub Release:
  https://github.com/HomesteadLink/firmware/releases/tag/v1.3
  Asset: homesteadlink-v1.3-orangepizero2w.img.xz, 559,467,796 bytes,
  SHA-256 ea0d155c2250c955dae0aab4c7ce57e080051891b51079047c07cf2fcc01f114.
  (Delivered via GitHub Release because the Cloudflare R2 path was
  blocked — the account has no R2 subscription.)
- v1.4.0 built 2026-11-15 with a FunctionFS USB vendor interface and
  the hsl-provisiond daemon (the USB transport the web app uses).
  Flash plus end-to-end test on real hardware is pending; the image
  merges to main only after the flash test proves it boots.

The SD-card swap is the only flash path. On-hardware boot is the final
arbiter — no claim of "works" without a boot on a real board.

Status (2026-11-16)
-------------------
- Firmware v1.3: delivered publicly (firmware#9 closed).
- Mobile app v1: built and emulator-tested; the P1–P16 physical session
  on a real board and phone is the remaining gate.
- Web app: live on GitHub Pages since 2026-11-15; all 6 screens verified
  by headless-Chrome screenshots, 0 console errors. Known v1 gap:
  Diagnostics is trigger-only (no download yet).
- Landing site: not live yet (https://homesteadlink.netlify.app is
  HTTP 404); deploy is blocked on a stale Netlify token only the owner
  can replace. No SEO work on the landing until it is live.
- Google Play: no listing yet. No Sentry project yet. Goal: 1M Google
  Play downloads; acceptance is good Play reviews, no open GitHub
  issues, and all repeated Sentry issues fixed fundamentally.
